svg.title: Ethersphere bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 supply chain kill chain
svg.desc: Single-lane chain of six stages: failed CI secret-dump probes and C2 domain registration on 2026-11-06; abuse of the bee-worker release identity to publish bee-js 13.3.0 through trusted publishing; postinstall loader executing remote JavaScript; signed Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 delivered by auto-update; wallet theft and Go or ScreenConnect backdoors; Ethereum dead-drop C2 and break points. Critical stages are the release abuse, the postinstall loader and the backdoor stage. Detection anchors are Sigma 01-04, KQL k1-k3, YARA, Suricata sids 9992001-9992005 and PEAK hunts H1-H3.
svg.text: bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2: trusted-publishing supply chain compromise
Vendor: Socket / StepSecurity (2026-11-09) | Date: 2026-11-12 | Cluster: unattributed, SleepyDuck-linked (medium) | Day 142
NPM, GITHUB ACTIONS, SWARM DESKTOP, 6-9 NOV 2026
Preparation 2026-11-06: failed CI secret-dump probes and C2 domain registration [T1583.001 T1195.002]
Probe branches ran workflows dumping toJSON(secrets) to webhook.site (Socket: no request body seen, moderate confidence)
Targets shifted from GitHub PATs to Apple and Windows signing material to NPM_TOKEN; the harvest failed
api.frameworkmetrics.xyz registered 2026-11-06 15:08 UTC (NICENIC); how the later credentials were obtained is unknown
branches probe/force-dryrun-* security/lab-secrets-* test-run api.frameworkmetrics[.]xyz
Release path abuse: unsigned commit and release under the bee-worker identity [T1195.002 T1078]
2026-11-08 23:59:54 UTC unsigned direct commit to the upcoming branch; release-please PR #1288 was still open
Release v13.3.0 at 00:06:01 UTC started the npm publish workflow, which needs no approval; published 00:09:50 UTC
Valid SLSA provenance: it proves where the package was built, not that anyone reviewed the code
commit de2f74e784b2eafa0d66fbb6d88b42ea11ee34cf @ethersphere/bee-js@13.3.0
bee-js 13.3.0 postinstall loader fetches and runs remote JavaScript [T1195.002 T1059.007]
package.json: prepare renamed to postinstall (node scripts/generate-version.cjs); loader on top of that file, no import needed
https.get to /v1/analytics with X-Ethersphere: 1 and User-Agent = platform; response run via new Function with require and process
Live on npm latest for about 75 minutes (until 01:24:58 UTC); dependents with open ranges: swarm-cli, bee-dashboard
[FrameworkMetrics] analytics v2.3.1 is up to date api.frameworkmetrics[.]xyz/v1/analytics
Swarm Desktop 0.56.2: signing workflow abused, signed release pushed by auto-update [T1195.002]
Manual pre-release.yml run (free-form branch, no environment protection) used Apple and Windows signing certs; macOS notarized
Updater offered 0.56.2 to Windows x64 and Apple Silicon from about 00:43 UTC; Intel Macs and Linux were not auto-updated
Loader in dist/desktop/src/index.js runs at every launch via /v1/electron; release withdrawn about 09:14 UTC
Bee Desktop version: 0.56.2 (production) Developer ID Swarm Association (9J9SPHU9RP)
Wallet theft and backdoors: Go shell on Linux/macOS, ScreenConnect on Windows [T1005 T1041 T1543 T1219]
config.yaml and data-dir/keys/swarm.key POSTed to /v1/swarm/report; keystore password sits in plaintext in config.yaml
Linux/macOS: ~/.solidity/ binary plus systemd user unit or LaunchAgent; Windows: silent ScreenConnect MSI, Defender exclusion
Windows service ScreenConnect Client (5cbe79c9c25524df) points to a relay; funds theft not established by the sources
~/.solidity/ solidity-langsupport-runner.service com.solidity.langsupport.runner 185.232.84[.]169:8041
Ethereum dead-drop C2 and break points [T1102.001 T1071.001]
Backdoor reads the hub from contract 0xf8a900...C344 via public RPC gateways (ankr, cloudflare-eth); operator can retarget at any time
Hub 193.57.9[.]155:4912 as of Nov 8; TLS without certificate validation; persistent sh pty shell
Break points: block lifecycle scripts, age-gate new releases, protect release workflows, rotate wallet and CI secrets, rebuild hosts
eth_call 0x02d91518 193.57.9[.]155:4912 rpc.ankr.com cloudflare-eth.com
Detection anchors
Sigma 01-04, KQL k1-k3, YARA (3 rules), Suricata sids 9992001-9992005, PEAK H1-H3. Hub IPs rotate; treat them as historical.
Break points: lifecycle-script policy, release-age gate, workflow approvals, ~/.solidity and ScreenConnect service checks, RPC eth_call hunts.
